correctness.rationale: For every fixed n, q times the derivative of expected total cycle count equals its covariance with inversion count. Direct two-arc completion yields exact covariance -(2n-1)/12 at q=1. The identity and reversal are the unique minimum- and maximum-inversion permutations; their n-1 adjacent-transposition neighbors give exact coefficients -(n-1) at q down to 0 and +a_n/q at q to infinity, with a_n=n-1 for odd n, n-3 for even n. Since a_n>0 for n>=3, continuity gives a zero strictly above q=1 and a local minimum of expected cycles. The n=2 exact rational formula excludes reversal; n=3 sign uniqueness follows from Descartes on the explicit quartic. verify.py checks n=2,...,8 exactly but is not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The theorem reveals a universal sign reversal between inversion bias and cycle count for the canonical Mallows ranking distribution. Its threshold is sharp across all sample sizes: n=2 has no reversal, every n>=3 does. The parity-dependent large-q coefficient identifies an exact structural mechanism involving the central two-cycle of the reverse permutation. It supplies a meaningful boundary to the intuitive but false monotonic decrease of cycle count as inversion bias increases, distinct from the already-known q=1 derivative.
